countries.name: Japan
countries.summary: A deep country for regional guessing: road infrastructure, utility poles, plates, reflectors, terrain, climate, and dense visual context all matter.
quick: Short white plates with green text; kei cars can use yellow plates

items.name: Utility-pole plates
items.text: Regional electrical-company plates are one of the strongest foundations for advanced Japan region guessing. The exact plate style varies by region.

items.name: Pole reflectors
items.text: Reflector-pad designs vary by region. Nationwide generic patterns also exist, so the full shape and placement matter.

items.name: Transformers and pole tops
items.text: Transformer mounts, crossbars, and attachments can provide regional information when combined with other pole features.

items.name: Licence plates
items.text: Standard plates are short and light-colored; kei cars commonly use a yellow plate variant. Treat this as supporting context rather than a region clue.

items.name: Road diamonds & signpost stickers
items.text: Some road-diamond styles and signpost stickers are regionally useful, especially at advanced levels.

items.name: Hokkaido pole hardware
items.text: Distinct transformer and pole-top arrangements can strongly support Hokkaido when seen clearly.

items.name: Shikoku & Kansai pole attachments
items.text: Characteristic pole attachments occur in these regions, but examples should be compared carefully before using them as a lock.

confusions.shared: Concrete poles, dense overhead wiring, mountainous roads, East Asian built environment
confusions.distinguish: Roadside hardware, scripts, pole-reflector style, driving/road context

confusions.shared: Dense utilities, similar urban textures in some areas
confusions.distinguish: Scripts, road furniture, plate/road context, pole-reflector design

countries.name: Ghana
countries.summary: A country with famous coverage clues, clear north–south landscape differences, and useful road/vegetation patterns.
quick: Distinctive Google-car clues on many coverages
Drier savannah north, denser vegetation south

items.name: Ghana tape
items.text: On regular generation-3 road coverage, a roof rack with black tape on the right side of the front bar is a highly distinctive clue.

items.name: Generation-4 pickup
items.text: Generation-4 imagery can show a grey or white pickup with a front antenna, often partly blurred.

items.name: North–south vegetation contrast
items.text: Northern Ghana trends toward drier savannah, while denser forests and palms are more common farther south and southwest.

items.name: Coastal palms
items.text: Tall palms are especially common near parts of the coast and can support a coastal read.

items.name: Black-and-white signposts
items.text: Black-and-white striped signposts are common in Ghanaian cities, but similar patterns exist elsewhere and need supporting context.

confusions.shared: Tropical African streetscapes and English-language context
confusions.distinguish: Google-car clues, road furniture, vegetation pattern

confusions.shared: West African urban and tropical visual texture
confusions.distinguish: Coverage clues and Street View availability/context

countries.name: Colombia
countries.summary: Strong national identifiers combine with huge geographic variety: Andes, Caribbean lowlands, tropical valleys, and major urban regions.
quick: Yellow licence plates are a major national clue
Distinctive signpost-back construction can be useful

items.name: Yellow licence plates
items.text: Yellow plates are one of Colombia’s strongest visual identifiers in South America when visible clearly.

items.name: Antenna / car context
items.text: Certain generation-3 and generation-4 car appearances can support Colombia, but similar antennas occur elsewhere in the Americas.

items.name: Cross-shaped signpost backs
items.text: White metal signposts often join in a characteristic cross shape behind signs. Similar white posts can occur elsewhere, so inspect the construction.

confusions.distinguish: Plate color, signpost construction, coverage and road context

confusions.shared: Some antenna and urban visual overlaps
confusions.distinguish: Yellow plates, vegetation/road context, sign hardware

countries.name: Guatemala
countries.summary: A compact but varied country with a very strong Street View vehicle clue, volcanic highlands, tropical lowlands, and distinct architecture.
quick: Grey Street View car with visible rack and mirrors

items.name: Guatemala car
items.text: Regular car coverage shows a grey vehicle with a visible roof rack and side mirrors, making this one of the country’s strongest clues.

items.name: Pastel masonry + sheet-metal roofs
items.text: A common architectural texture, especially useful when combined with terrain, road quality, and the Google car.

items.name: Lake Atitlán landscape
items.text: A large highland lake surrounded by steep mountains and volcanoes creates a distinctive regional environment.

confusions.shared: A superficially similar visible-car/rack impression can occur in tropical coverage
confusions.distinguish: Driving side, language, architecture, road environment

confusions.shared: Visible-car impression can confuse at a glance

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.summary: Dense subtropical development, Traditional Chinese, scooters, mountain roads, and detailed utility infrastructure make Taiwan highly learnable through visual combinations.
quick: Dense scooter presence in many urban areas

items.name: Utility-pole identification
items.text: Pole labels and infrastructure can become regionally useful. Taiwan-specific pole study is especially valuable for advanced players.

items.name: Pole reflector distinction
items.text: Reflector-pad styling can help separate Taiwan from Japan and South Korea when seen clearly.

items.name: County-level practice
items.text: Road prefixes, area codes, and pole information can all support county-level study once national identification is secure.

confusions.shared: Mountain roads, concrete utility poles, dense overhead wires, East Asian streetscapes
confusions.distinguish: Script, driving side, scooter prevalence, roadside and pole hardware

confusions.shared: Urban density and some utility textures
confusions.distinguish: Script, road markings, scooters, vegetation and architecture
